devon: Quick question — when we choose FP8 kernel for attention, are we fusing dequant per-head or after concat? Observed a big memory spike on 32k context on A100s.

sasha: We currently do per-tensor dequant before matmul, but per-head would avoid keeping separate int tensors around. The RFC had perf numbers: https://r.redwood/rfcs/quant-attn-v2 — TLDR: per-head reduces peak by ~20% for long contexts.

maria: Per-head helps with KV cache layout too, because we can keep KV in INT8 slab and only expand when we do the matmul. But it complicates kernel ABI and the register pressure.

kevin: ABI concerns: how do we express fused-dequant kernel vs splitter? Proposal: kernel metadata flags: {accepts_int_kv, supports_inplace_dequant, layout_version}. Runtime then picks by capability.

alex: +1 on flags. Example runtime policy (pseudocode):
```
if model.quant == "FP8" and device.supports_fp8_fused:
  use_kernel("attn_fp8_fused")
elif model.quant == "INT8" and device.fast_dequant:
  use_kernel("attn_int8_splitter")
else:
  fallback("fp32_attn")
```

maria: Also need to handle KV cache growth: fused path must be able to append int shards without copying. Otherwise we lose the bandwidth win.

devon: Right — current implementation forces a copy when switching from fused->non-fused because of layout mismatch, and that kills tail latency spikes.

infra-bot: deploy:quant-kernel-cc-2 started by @kevin at 1715702000

sasha: Could we define a tiny on-disk/header in KV slab indicating layout_version and quant_format? Then runtime can mmap and avoid copies by remapping or choosing an adapter kernel.

kevin: Header idea ok but adds ~16 bytes per slab header; seems acceptable vs copying large tensors. Need to think about alignment.

maria: Also cost tradeoff: FP8 fused reduces bandwidth by ~2x but sometimes increases compute due to more complex instructions. Measured ~1.9x token/sec on single GPU microbench for sampled configs.

alex: Edge-case: A/B rollout — prefer safe fallback that switches to FP32 per-request rather than global offline rewrite. Per-tenant policy is important.

devon: Agree — prefer per-request routing with per-tenant policy flags: prefer_low_latency vs prefer_cost. That maps to routing rules: prefer fused if latency not worsened.

sasha: Action items from this thread: 1) update kernel ABI RFC with flags + layout_version 2) add KV slab header spec 3) add runtime routing test that simulates 32k contexts and slab growth.

maria: I'll pick up #2 (KV header spec).

kevin: I'll take #1 and open a PR to kernel registry + sample ABI docs.

sasha: I'll add the 32k context test to the runtime test harness and a stress scenario for dequant fallback.

kevin: FYI I'm going to prototype a small adapter kernel that can do on-the-fly head-wise dequant in-place to avoid copies. If it works we can mark supports_inplace_dequant.

infra-bot: CI:quant-kernel-tests passed in 12m by @sasha (build 4821)

devon: OK let's sync in the eng-runtime sync tomorrow 10:00 PT. Thanks all :rocket:
